entry.title: Phonon-assisted free-electron recoil control and mechanical sensing
entry.summary:
Mechanical vibrations are fundamental to a wide range of physical phenomena and technologies, yet their ability to actively shape free-electron dynamics remains largely unexplored. Here we theoretically show how an optomechanical membrane provides a phonon-assisted optical interface for controlling free-electron recoil and sensing localized forces. Transverse membrane motion scatters cavity light into high-momentum evanescent sidebands that enable phase-matched interaction with electrons traveling in vacuum.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #optics-photonics #high-energy

entry.title: Superconductivity and ferroelectric orbital magnetism in semimetallic rhombohedral hexalayer graphene
entry.summary:
Nature Physics, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03443-9 The semimetallic regime in rhombohedral graphene has not been extensively explored. Now, correlated insulators, superconductivity and multiferroic orbital magnetic order are demonstrated in semimetallic rhombohedral hexalayer graphene.

Source: Nature Physics · Tags: #quantum-physics #optics-photonics #combinatorics #condensed-matter

entry.title: Coherent phonon control beyond amplitude saturation in a sliding ferroelectric
entry.summary:
Nature Physics, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03491-1 Strong photoexcitation of phonons in a crystal can lead to a nonlinear response. Now it is shown that this breakdown of linearity can be overcome by the application of well-timed photoexcitation pulses in WTe2.

Source: Nature Physics · Tags: #quantum-physics #optics-photonics

entry.title: Fibres and glasses are competing material states in protein condensation
entry.summary:
Nature Physics, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03415-z Fibres are thought to emerge from a dense protein condensate ageing into a glassy state. It is now shown that protein fibres and glassy condensates may result from two competing ageing pathways.

Source: Nature Physics · Tags: #quantum-physics #optics-photonics #genomics-proteins
